source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text:
In the rush at the counter, bags slide swiftly along the conveyer, while a scanner whirs quietly. Behind them, a divider bars off the bagging area. A cashier types away on the register; next to her, a shopper’s cart juts out into the line.

Nearby, another shopper shoves forward impatiently, creating a slight tussle for space. The routine of retail ticks along: beeps sound as items are scanned, and the total is announced with clarity. A loyalty-card prompt flashes on the screen, inviting engagement.

At my turn, I place my groceries carefully onto the conveyor belt. The barcode scanner reads each item, and the bagger deftly stows them into a plastic bag. My loyalty card slides across the card reader, collecting points as usual.

As the line flows, another shopper hovers just beyond the divider, eager for their turn. The friction of queuing becomes palpable in these moments of crowding. Yet, the rhythm of the register's operations maintains its steady pace: beeps, totals, loyalty prompts—each a part of our everyday retail ballet.

In the line at the bustling market, the conveyor's gentle hum carried items under the scanner. A shopper slid a cart past the divider bar, their face illuminated by the receipt printer. Behind them, another pushed close, nearly spilling groceries. The cashier beeps rang out as each item was added to her screen, the total clearly announced, and loyalty-card prompts flashed. 

The customer handed over change while the next line began its own cycle: a crisp beep, an item scanned, and the register's steady voice giving another sum. The bagging area hummed with activity, bags being tied and placed in front of waiting customers. Over by the card reader, another shopper tapped their card, eyes on the screen. 

The first shopper moved to the end of the line, the conveyor quieting as they turned to retrieve their purchases from the belt. Behind them, another stepped up, the divider bar swinging out with a soft clack. Beeps sounded again in syncopation, a constant rhythm of retail exchange.

As the second customer finished, the cashier pushed back their cart and joined the now longer line. Another shopper edged forward, pressing closer to the conveyor belt as it moved forward. The beeps from scanning added to the sound of busy hands and soft chatter. 

In the line's steady flow, each transaction was a momentary pause in a larger stream: beep, scan, total, hand over cash or card. The friction between customers was minimal, a shared understanding of space in a busy queue.

Beneath the counter, stacks of barcodes, each a rectangle of potential, awaited their turn like soldiers in a long line.

A shopper slid his cart under the narrow divider, the conveyor belt humming to life with its mechanical rhythm. 

Behind him, another approached, pushing a second cart into the space, causing a brief friction where they nearly touched. The cashier, attentive, tapped the barcode scanner and the beeps began to echo, announcing each item as it crossed.

"Total comes to sixty-four," she called out clearly over her headset.

A loyalty-card prompt appeared on the screen, inviting the shopper's swipe. He reached into his bag for the card, pulling it out with a fumble that nearly sent his groceries tumbling.

At the register, retail routine played out: the beeps, the total announced, and the prompt to use a loyalty card.

At the bustling line, the belt carried items past the scanner, and the bagger prepared the bags while the card reader stood by. In front of me, the cashier's eyes were fixed on her screen as she tapped away. My cart was pushed close to the divider bar, and I held my receipt waiting.

From behind, another shopper pressed forward, bumping lightly against the back of my cart. "Excuse me," they muttered, though it wasn't needed.

"Beep beep beep," went the scanner for each item added. The total flashed up: four dollars sixty-five. "Use your loyalty card to save," the machine prompted as the cashier offered a smile and handed over change in crisp notes.

Behind us, more shoppers waited impatiently, their carts jostling ever so slightly. An elderly woman pushed her own cart, the handle barely clearing the ground with each push. Her receipt was placed neatly beside mine.

"Two dollars eighty-seven," she read aloud, then paused to check the total again before handing over her card. The cashier nodded and printed her receipt. As we moved towards the exit, I noticed another shopper crowding up behind us, their cart pressing into my back.

"Just two more items, please," the cashier requested, gesturing towards me to help speed along the process. "Sure," I replied, reaching for the last item in my bag, feeling a small friction in the queue as we all tried to move smoothly together.

In line six, crates slide past the scanner, each a world on its own. Alongside, shelves of items await, an orderly chaos. Next to the cashier, a cart stands divided from the queue by a barrier, ready for the bagger's touch. Another shopper inches closer, pushing gently, a subtle tug at space. The register hums with beeps as items are scanned, each one adding to the total—a digital whisper of retail routine. Loyalty-card prompts flash softly, offering points and savings. 

By the eighth item, the belt slows down, a momentary stillness in motion. A small friction arises from the crowd behind; hands brush lightly against the divider, a silent tussle for place. The cashier checks each barcode with practiced precision, announcing totals with a steady voice. Cards are swiped, and the world of scanned goods feels like a ritual, a dance between machine and human.

Near the tenth item, the line moves forward again, the scan beeping out the final number. Shoppers step back into the aisle, bags in hand, greeted by receipts that flutter like paper butterflies from the printer. The routine hums on, the beeps of the scanner merging with the chime of shopping carts being wheeled away.

In the long queue at the supermarket, the conveyor belt hummed steadily while the barcode scanner whirred by. The bagging area was close to the cashier where a shopper had placed their cart, with a divider bar for separation from another person crowding in from behind. 

Beside the register, the loyalty-card prompts flickered occasionally as shoppers swiped their cards. The total beeps out loud when the cashier finished entering items, and they reminded everyone to place the receipt on the conveyor belt. Another shopper tried to squeeze closer but faced a small friction over space, causing minor tension in the queue.

At the counter, the cashier worked methodically while the scanner buzzed each barcode, confirming prices as they rang up purchases one by one. The noise of beeps and announcements filled the air as more customers approached, adding to the busy hour atmosphere at the checkout line.

The conveyor belt carried out bags with efficiency, each item bagged neatly before being placed on a rack for pickup. As people got their receipts, the cashier prompted them to swipe their cards for any ongoing promotions or savings programs that might apply. 

Despite the steady stream of activity and occasional disputes over space, the routine of the checkout process continued smoothly, punctuated by beeps and announcements as items were tallied up on the register.

The division between the shoppers seemed clear but sometimes blurred when new customers arrived at the busy queue. The cashier maintained a steady pace while reminding everyone to keep their distance from each other for safety and efficiency's sake during this hour of peak traffic at the supermarket checkout line.

With every beep, another purchase was confirmed, and the total announced over the speaker as bags were filled with items. Another shopper approached cautiously, knowing they would be joining the queue soon; already, a minor friction existed between the shoppers due to limited space in the busy hour.

The familiar routine of retail continued, each step carefully managed by the cashier while customers waited their turn at the conveyor belt, scanned barcodes, and had their items bagged. The card reader was used diligently for loyalty rewards, with beeps indicating each successful scan as the total amount was announced loudly over the register's speaker.

As another customer joined the queue, a brief moment of tension arose due to the squeeze caused by an overcrowded line at the supermarket checkout during this busy hour. The cashier continued working efficiently while the conveyor belt kept humming steadily in the background.

In the bustling line, a cart's contents slid smoothly on the conveyor belt to the barcode scanner. Behind stood another shopper, eager for their turn. The divider bar separated them, and the cashier waited at the register.

At each beep, items were added to the total. A loyalty-card prompt flashed as the shopper scanned theirs. The other customer pressed in closer, pushing against the cart with a small friction. "Excuse me," one said, irritated, but it was too late for space. 

The shopper's name popped up on the screen; their order confirmed and bagged. The card reader beeped, accepting payment from a preloaded account. Meanwhile, another item arrived at the scanner.

"Here you go," the cashier said, extending the receipt. "Thanks." With that, they moved to the next customer, the line shifting slightly.

At the end of their turn, the loyalty-card prompt would appear again for any points earned. The next shopper approached, ready to start their own retail routine.

In the crowded line, a cart rested against the divider bar, and a shopper held up a barcode, case by case, detaching items with precise movements; the conveyor belt hummed softly beneath them. Near the end of the queue stood another figure, a small friction over who would next step forward.

The cashier's hand hovered over the register as it beeped each item, the total announced clearly before the shopper could speak. A loyalty-card prompt flashed momentarily, but was swiftly ignored.

At the register, a bundle of pencils caught the scanner's eye, each one beeping in turn as they were added to the total. The shopper fumbled for change, the cashier leaning forward slightly with patient interest.

The line moved steadily, each item processed by the machine with precise efficiency. Another pack of tissues slid into place, its weight a silent judgment between the two.

Nearby, someone cleared their throat gently; the tension was palpable but brief. The register continued to hum softly as it worked through each object.

A packet of sugar clicked into position within reach; the moment passed without incident, the queue continuing on its course.

The cashier leaned back slightly, the total recited once more before any action was taken. A loyalty-card prompt appeared again, but this time, the shopper reached for their card with a nod of understanding.

A final item—tea bags—dropped into place; the line moved forward seamlessly as the transaction concluded.

At the edge, near the divider bar, the cart nudged gently against the queue's flow; a whisper of friction stirred between the shopper and another crowding from behind. Beeps from the conveyor belt and the barcode scanner mingled with the cashier’s announcements of totals; loyalty-card prompts echoed softly in the background.

The cashier, focused intently, nimbly moved items into bags, while the shopper placed cards into a slot beside the register. Numbers flashed on the screen, each beep a small pulse of transactional routine. Another customer squeezed closer to the divider, nudging slightly as the line stretched longer.

The conveyor belt glided smoothly beneath the scanner, and the bagger deftly arranged items within the bag, ensuring none were left behind. The loyalty-card slot read it, triggering a prompt for points; the total appeared on the screen in large, clear numbers before the cashier spoke out loud, "That comes to three twenty-five."

The small divider bar stood as a silent boundary between transactions, separating one queue from another. As the card reader clicked, indicating completion, the next shopper's voice whispered behind, demanding more space; the line adjusted ever so slightly with each passing moment.

At last, it was the cashier’s turn to announce, "Next!" The register beeped quietly as the cart pulled away from the edge of the queue, another transaction concluded in the busy supermarket routine.
